description: Verify that DUT learns from a received ARP Request and uses the cached MAC for the next UDP egress — but only after first emitting its own ARP Request to claim the address pair (RFC 826 §2.3 + RFC 5227 ACD probe semantics)
approach:
[Objective]
This case is the harness's primary witness for receive-side learning + send-side use. RFC 826 §2.3 says learn from sender_ip/sender_mac; harness convention adds: DUT must ALSO emit its own ARP Request first (announcing presence) before unicasting UDP. Pass requires both behaviours in the right order.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • sender_ip = HOST-1-IP, sender_mac = MAC-ADDR1
   • target_ip = DUT IP
   ⇒ DUT learns <HOST-1-IP, MAC-ADDR1>.

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup
   ⇒ stimulates DUT to send a UDP response.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   a. DUT → broadcast: DUT's own ARP Request (announces its iface mapping)
   b. After (a), DUT → Tester: UDP with eth_dst == MAC-ADDR1 (the learned value)

[Pass condition]
Both (a) and (b) observed, in this order, and UDP eth_dst == MAC-ADDR1.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_dut_request — DUT skipped its own announcement Request
• Fail_udp_before_dut_request — DUT sent UDP without first announcing — order violated
• Fail_wrong_eth_dst — UDP eth_dst was not MAC-ADDR1 (cache entry not used)
• Fail_no_udp — DUT did not emit UDP within the window

verdicts.Pass: DUT announced via own Request, then sent UDP using learned MAC — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_dut_request: DUT did not announce via own Request
verdicts.Fail_udp_before_dut_request: DUT sent UDP before its own Request — order violated
verdicts.Fail_wrong_eth_dst: UDP eth_dst was not the learned MAC — cache not used
verdicts.Fail_no_udp: DUT did not emit UDP within the window
